# Non-audio MEDIA export authoring requests (not proof)

`native-specs.json` **first** defines eleven independent AE source requests. All
sources, exports and measurements are **UNRUN / uninspected / unmeasured**. No
native `.aep`, composition ID/source hash, Adobe-rendered 30fps MP4, long-term
Asset, Adobe acceptance or independent comparison is claimed. Do not register
an invented ID/hash or use an FX-exported AEP as the native reference.

`panel-registry.json` gives every case ID, exact test symbol and explicit edited
FX/hand-authored expected-contract paths. The structural test is
`src/export_document/tests/media_native_panel.rs`; the parent must register it
in `tests.rs` under the existing opt-in feature. The test packages actual
primary media via `TesseractFileBuilder`, fresh-exports FX→AEP, asserts native
editable sources/layer ranges, media descriptors and byte-identical publication,
and checks contextual omissions. The fixed converter-workspace scratch directory
`target/adobe-test/fx_exports/` receives `<case>.fx.json`,
`<case>.expected.json`, `<case>.aep`, and standalone `<case>/project.aep` plus
`<case>/media/` for Adobe; only the separately authored `native/<case-id>.aep`
will be an independent oracle. No import assertion is supplied here.

Primary stills are real uncompressed scanline EXRs authored deterministically by
`make_media.py`: dominant red/green opposing checker patterns, 64×48. The
unsupported bright-orange PNG is separately generated by the same standard-
library authoring script; it must be diagnosed and omitted while red survives.
`media/movie.mov` is a byte-for-byte copy of `../audio_e2e/movie.mov`, the
independently authored eight-second 320×180/24fps blue MOV (with audio disabled
on the video occurrences). Preserve original bytes, hash and pin before Adobe
production; no converter-generated media or reference is used.

| Case suffix | Export control / critical structural claim | Native visual qualification |
|---|---|---|
| image-fit | OpenEXR descriptor, Cover-frame crop mask and keyed opacity | Compare before/after 1s; opacity/alpha separately unverified by RGB MP4 |
| video-clock | QuickTime descriptor, source-in 0.5s and 0–2s trim | Blue source is static: clocks need independent native UI readback, not just blue frames |
| video-stretch | 2× affine source speed (0.25–4.25s), exact start/stretch | MOV is static blue: timing visually nondiscriminating; no visual fidelity pass |
| frame-blending | Frame Mix layer flag and comp master | Static blue cannot prove actual blend pixels; structural-only until moving source |
| shared-source | Two occurrences reuse one media item | Original blue source bytes pinned, two different positions/scales |
| source-switch | Red→green at 1s, held asset selector, two editable footage occurrences | Contrasting media is discriminating across boundary; native has independent child comp, not an FX-writer round trip |
| unsupported-sibling | PNG diagnosed/omitted, supported red retained/published | Native source only contains retained red sibling; omission has no visual-fidelity claim |
| static-remap | Native editable frozen sample at 0.75s | Blue is static: cannot visually prove remapping without moving source |
| image-3d | Stored position/orientation/opacity plus 3D layer flag | 3D projection/camera parity unverified |
| constant-source | Effective green descriptor, stale red asset not published | Red→green contrasts edited source and persisted old identity |
| legacy-image | Legacy Media still, EXR descriptor/stretch/opacity | Legacy support remains bounded to current supported controls |

**Not supplied in this panel:** referenced-as-parent/matte source-variant wrapper
and reminted children, custom-fit inverse crop and authored mask ordering, image
takeover slide (and unsupported video tail), 3D animated channels, optical-flow
frame-blending master propagation into nested groups, and nonlinear playback
rejection diagnostics. Those need their own pinned, discriminating native sources
and explicit export assertions; the supplementary PR #4442 structural tests do
not constitute Adobe proof. No broad feature-completion claim follows from the
11 source requests. Adobe production must preserve native composition 24fps,
render at 30fps for full 2s, inspect critical frames, publish immutable
long-term media Asset and freshly verify SHA. Keep MP4s out of Git.
